Expectation1: Adhere to site protocols and work effectively as part of the team.
Situation1: The mandatory daily pre-work safety briefing is starting in two minutes.
Expectation2: Support individuals or groups in accessing essential services and resources
Situation2: They assist someone who is struggling with paperwork or procedures needed to receive public support.
Story: I wipe the sweat from my brow as the foreman’s voice crackles over the loudspeaker, reminding everyone that the safety briefing starts in two minutes. My boots are caked with dust, and I know if I’m late, the team will see me as unreliable—maybe even careless. But my phone buzzes in my pocket. It’s Maria, the single mother I’ve been helping as an advocate. She’s at the social services office, panicked and overwhelmed by the forms she needs to fill out to keep her benefits. She’s pleading for help, her voice trembling through the text. I glance at the gathering crew, the expectation clear: be present, be focused, be part of the team. But Maria needs me now, and I promised I’d support her when she felt lost. My heart pounds as I stand at the crossroads, torn between the rules of the site and the trust of someone counting on me.
